blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
International tax happens when a deal crosses a border. If a company in the UK sells services to a client in Brazil, both countries may have some right to tax the income.

How much each country takes depends on their laws and on the treaties they sign with each other. The rules are hard, but the idea is simple: when money moves between countries, someone has to decide who taxes what. Treaties stop the same income being taxed twice in full.

International tax is not a problem for a small domestic business. But the moment a company sells abroad, it quietly becomes part of a wider, more formal system.

items.q: When does international tax happen?
options: When a business pays its rent
When a company opens a bank account
When a company hires new staff
When a deal crosses a border
items.why: "International tax happens when a deal crosses a border."

items.q: What decides how much each country takes?
options: Their laws and the treaties they sign
items.why: "How much each country takes depends on their laws and on the treaties they sign."

items.q: What do treaties stop?
options: The same income being taxed twice in full
items.why: "Treaties stop the same income being taxed twice in full."

items.q: The text suggests that a small business selling only at home…
options: does not face international tax yet
items.why: Inferência: "not a problem for a small domestic business" — só entra nesse sistema quando vende para fora.

items.q: The word "quietly" suggests that the company…
options: makes a lot of noise about the change
joins the bigger system without really noticing
items.why: Inferência: "quietly becomes part" — a mudança acontece sem barulho, quase sem a empresa perceber.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James explicar a situação para o cliente. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
So, congratulations on the new contract with your customer in Brazil. It is great news. But I want to talk to you about one small thing before it grows into a big thing.

Until now, all your clients were here in the UK. You sold at home, you paid tax at home, and life was simple. This new deal is different. The money crosses a border, so two countries — the UK and Brazil — may both have a right to tax the income.

Please do not worry. This does not mean you pay tax twice in full. The two countries have a treaty, and the treaty decides how they share the tax. That is exactly what treaties are for.

What I need from you is simple. Send me the contract and tell me who signs the invoice. With that, I can explain the numbers clearly. You have not done anything wrong. You have just grown into a wider, more formal system, and I am here to guide you through it.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why is this new deal different from the client's past deals?
items.why: "The money crosses a border, so two countries may both have a right to tax the income."

items.q: What does James ask the client to send him?
options: The contract and who signs the invoice
items.why: "Send me the contract and tell me who signs the invoice."

items.q: According to James, does the client pay tax twice in full?
options: No, the treaty shares the tax
items.why: "This does not mean you pay tax twice in full… the treaty decides how they share the tax."

items.q: How does James most likely want the client to feel?
items.why: Inferência: ele diz "Please do not worry" e "I am here to guide you" — quer tranquilizar.

items.q: What does James suggest about selling abroad?
options: It brings new rules the client did not have before
It is always a bad idea
It is exactly the same as selling at home
items.why: Inferência: "grown into a wider, more formal system" — vender fora traz regras novas que não existiam em casa.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "The sale crossed a border." A border is…
items.why: Border = fronteira, a linha entre dois países.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Both countries may have a ___ to tax this income."
items.why: Right to tax = direito de tributar.

items.q: "The two countries signed a treaty." A treaty is…
items.why: Treaty = tratado, um acordo formal entre países.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "They must follow the tax ___ of both countries."
items.why: Law = lei; "tax laws" são as leis de imposto.

items.q: "A small domestic business" is a business that…
options: sells only inside its own country
items.why: Domestic = doméstico; aqui, que vende só dentro do próprio país.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em conversas de negócios sobre impostos. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager still has to sign off on the invoice." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new tax process next month." To roll out means to…
options: start using it step by step
items.why: Roll out = começar a usar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "The client pushed back on the extra fee." This means the client…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "They agreed to send the contract but never followed through." They…
options: did not finish what they promised
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's sort out the tax before the deal closes." To sort out means to…
items.why: Sort out = resolver, organizar algo.
